key_insight: Kriging and neural-network models can accurately predict pressure loss across perforated plates in turbulent flow, outperforming standard empirical formulas.
engineering_relevance: These data-driven models offer a practical way to improve pressure-drop estimation in CFD and design calculations for perforated-plate systems.
method: Trained two surrogate models, one using kriging and one using neural networks, on experimental pressure-loss datasets.
Compared model predictions against common empirical correlations for multiple perforated-plate configurations.
Implemented the new pressure-loss models as momentum source terms in 2D RANS channel-flow simulations.
evidence_signal: Using two literature-based experimental datasets, both models showed good agreement with measurements and generally outperformed widely used empirical formulas.
watch_item: The models were trained on a relatively limited amount of experimental data, so extrapolation beyond the tested perforation geometries and flow conditions should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Kriging and neural network models for pressure losses across perforated plates
